report:
Reviewed the complete identity_only claim, all four implementation associations and sole TODO test; captured the resolution design. Source inspection only, without test reruns or source edits.

The claim confines ordinary lookup to identity/completeness information and prohibits hidden receiver inference, associated-type normalization, obligation proof or applicable-method selection. resolve_path returns lexical Resolution entries or symbol identities discovered through module/import edges. ribs.rs lookup copies an existing Local, Param, Sym or SelfTy entry; returning an already supplied SelfTy is not inferring a receiver. symbol.rs children enters only modules/enums, while named_children filters external membership by name and namespace and constructs canonical symbols. Path continuation walks those identity containers; it does not reinterpret a type parameter path as a normalized associated type or invoke a method candidate checker. The existing FIXME about T::Item denotes an unsupported lookup extension, not a hidden call into inference.

The surrounding resolver tracks conservative completeness in method-scope provider discovery, returning discovered identities and its completeness flag. The ordinary resolve_path API itself remains Vec<Resolution>; this inspection does not claim it implements a uniform structured completeness result for every ordinary path. The current architectural separation is identity discovery before downstream semantic selection; full result/completeness behavior remains part of the broader resolution verification work. No inference, trait-solver, selected-signature or checked-body operation was found in the associated ordinary lookup path.

The sole resolution_lookup_identity_only test is explicitly TODO with no assertions. It requires normalized representative lookup traces limited to searched scopes, imports and symbol/metadata identities, excluding inference, solver, candidate-signature and body work. Completing that trace matrix is prerequisite to full verification, including completeness propagation and unsupported associated paths. I do not promote absence of obvious calls or implementation annotations into proof of every transitive lookup route. All implementation entries and forbidden-operation categories are accounted for, with evidence honestly deferred; no concrete additional hidden semantic operation was identified and no edits are requested.
